limitations: Windows PowerShell 5.1 only: PowerShell 7 is not installed on this host, so no dual-engine claim is made for this binding.
Isolated fixtures on the verifying host; no external Server, IIS/SMB/PKI, business or scale acceptance (externalStatus stays not-tested).
Percentage is computed only during capture (capped at 99%); verification and delivery have no fine-grained data.
BytesTotal is known only after sealing.
200% zoom is emulated (640 CSS px, DPR 2), not a real browser zoom.
F1AcceptanceBrowser uses a stateful API double with the real src/ui and real PowerShell generators.
P4 (17.97) failed-item source path and P2 (17.95) partial-index preservation are exercised only through their own tests, not through the F1 acceptance screens.

P9 (17.101): a matching content hash does not prove the file was written by the tool, so a file placed beforehand with identical content is adopted and a later rollback may delete it (accepted risk); the single-file scope (RelativePath empty) adoption path is implemented but not tested; the P9 end-to-end test waits 16 seconds to avoid NTFS file tunneling.

P8 (17.100): failure Status values were exercised only with synthetic input and an IIS double, the real HTTP /api/operations path is not run (G4 simulates it in process through ConvertTo-WsmHtmlArguments), and the browser suite uses a fixed API stub. P8 and P9 tests were added to this stage by the mechanical rule that a stage whose inputs hold a changed src file runs them, so the attribution may be wider than the true dependency.
openIssues: The single cross-role checklist from inventory through verification is deliberately not built (user decision 2026-10-23, PLAN 17.83); the ledger keeps F1 in-progress.
Real-machine acceptance of the F1 screens (real zoom, assistive technology) is not collected.
